id: title:carlos-marchal-ph:stop counting displayed errors as session friction

review.posthog_relevance: Clarifies the expected behavior of the AI summarizer regarding friction detection, but this is a comment, not an implementation.
review.reason: The change adds documentation comments to a Jin2 template used for generating AI prompts. It distinguishes between user-visible friction and background errors, but no executable behavior, implementation, or PostHog mechanism is demonstrated. This is a documentation-only update.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a Jin2 template file used to generate prompts for an AI summarizer. The change adds a paragraph of comments explaining the distinction between friction points on a standard user-facing page versus a monitoring/support surface. This is documentation within the prompt template, not executable code. No implementation, behavior change, or PostHog mechanism is demonstrated

observations.behavior: Added explanatory comments distinguishing friction detection on standard UIs from monitoring/support surfaces.
observations.code_quote: - `friction_points`: list of named blockers, errors, or frustrations the user hit (empty if none). Only include things the user would notice — visible error states, dead clicks, rage clicks, abandoned actions, page reloads. Background JS console errors that don't affect the UI (ResizeObserver loops, feature-flag fetch failures, third-party script noise) are not friction. Neither is error content the product exists to display: on a monitoring, logging, tracing, exception, or support surface, the errors on screen are the data the user came to read, so reading them is the product working. On those surfaces, record friction only when the product itself failed the user — it didn't load, it didn't accept an action, or it 404'd.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies the expected behavior of the AI summarizer regarding friction detection, but this is a comment, not an implementation.
